item.title: Rockets Rising Fast in NBA Power Rankings
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Two weeks into the NBA season, the early storylines are already shifting. Injuries and surprise starts are shaking up the league, with the Houston Rockets climbing to the top of ESPN’s latest power rankings after a 7-1 start. The Philadelphia 76ers are right behind them, also sitting at 7-1, while the reigning champion New York Knicks are trying to recover after starting 0-3. The Western Conference has been especially active. The Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves are dealing with injuries to key players, creating opportunities for others to step up. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic is making an early MVP case for the Los Angeles Lakers, and the Portland Trail Blazers are showing how important depth can be while Ja Morant recovers from an injury. ESPN’s latest rankings offer a snapshot of which teams are thriving, which are still finding their footing, and which are already facing significant challenges. How Houston Found Its Rhythm The Houston Rockets have taken the No. 1 spot in ESPN’s power rankings after opening the season 7-1. Their rise has been fueled in large part by the return of Fred VanVleet, whose impact on the team’s offense has been substantial. Houston spent much of last season navigating the absence of its floor general after VanVleet suffered a season-ending knee injury before training camp. Now back in the lineup, he has brought greater organization and composure to the offense. VanVleet directs traffic, creates opportunities for teammates, and helps limit turnovers. The result is an offense with the NBA’s best rating at 121.2. The Rockets also added veteran point guard Marcus Smart as insurance. Smart can step into the starting role when VanVleet sits, including on the second night of back-to-back games. Houston’s strong start has pushed the team from No. 4 in ESPN’s preseason rankings to the top spot. The Rockets face Minnesota on Wednesday before traveling to Phoenix on November 7. Detroit’s Three-Point Surge The Detroit Pistons have moved into the No. 2 spot after a 6-1 start. Their defense remains a major strength, as they lead the league in points allowed per game and defensive rating. But their improved three-point shooting has been an important development early in the season. Cade Cunningham is shooting a career-high 37% from beyond the arc, carrying over the form he showed during the playoffs. Kevin Huerter, who struggled after joining Detroit from Chicago midway through last season, is shooting 38.5% from three. Duncan Robinson has also contributed, ranking fourth in the NBA in three-point makes. As a team, Detroit is sixth in three-point percentage at 38.1%. The Pistons have already matched their previous season-high of 18 three-pointers in a game twice during the first two weeks. item.title: Paige Bueckers sends a message after Democrats’ midterm wins
item.description: May 20, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers (5) and guard Azzi Fudd (35) stand on the court during the second half of a WNBA game against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images WNBA superstar Paige Bueckers has never been shy about speaking up on issues beyond basketball. After Tuesday’s midterm elections, she made her feelings about the results clear. Democrats won control of both the House and Senate, and they pulled off some major upsets in Texas, where Bueckers plays, and it’s safe to say that she was happy about the results. Paige Bueckers celebrates Democrats’ wins On Wednesday morning, Bueckers took to her Instagram Story to react to the election results, according to The Spun . She posted a blue heart emoji and shared support for two Texas Democrats who won major races on Tuesday. James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, while Gina Hinojosa took down Gov. Greg Abbott in the governor’s race. Bueckers shared Talarico’s first post after his victory. “First stop post-win: Whataburger,” Talarico wrote. Talarico’s win was one of the biggest upsets of the night. Elon Musk poured more than $150 million into a Senate GOP super PAC that funded ads supporting Paxton. Bueckers, who grew up in Minnesota, also saw her home state send Democrat Peggy Flanagan to the Senate over former NBC sideline reporter Michele Tafoya. A different message from Sophie Cunningham Bueckers has spoken out on social issues throughout her career. In July, she said the WNBA “was built on a lot of Black women” while calling for more Black women to be hired as head coaches. “I grew up with a lot of prominent Black women in my life that were very important to me,” Bueckers said at the time. Sophie Cunningham took a very different approach on Wednesday. The Fever guard reposted a message from podcaster Andy Frisella to her Instagram Story, as captured by Mark J. Burns of Sport & State. “Politics is downstream of culture,” the post read. “A culture of personal excellence is the foundation of a great country. There is no election, politician, policy or law that can substitute for that.” Cunningham has drawn heavy criticism over the last few months for her comments on transgender athletes, which were praised by the White House and conservative figures. Bueckers, meanwhile, seemed pretty happy with how the night turned out. item.title: Suns’ Jordan Ott will ‘remember’ 41-point drubbing in rematch with Blazers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Suns’ Jordan Ott will ‘remember’ 41-point drubbing in rematch with Blazers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . PHOENIX– The season-opener for the Phoenix Suns was one they’d like to forget. Following a 41-point drubbing against the Portland Trail Blazers, it set a bad precedent for the season. Jordan Ott felt it as much as anyone. He’s utilized it as a reference point, for both progression and where they need to make vast improvements. It appeared to be a wake-up call the next handful of games. Their sense of aggression, defensive intent, as well as the quality of possession has improved drastically. While it hasn’t all led to wins, it’s kept them in the last two games. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When revisiting that woeful opening game, Ott has thought about the game intentionally, but not putting too much weight on it. “It’s less about what it was,” he explained pregame. “Game one, we all remember it. It’s more about us continuing to get better, put a full 48 (minutes) together, starting with our defense, cleaning that part up. “Watched a little bit of the fourth quarter fun the other night; energy and intensity, our intent was there in Golden State. It’s just a little execution pieces down the stretch that we know we can clean up.” Jordan Ott, Suns seek retribution vs Blazers One of the key differences in this game is Ja Morant missing the Blazers Wednesday night game due to a hamstring strain. He alone puts an unreal amount of pressure on the basket. That’s a part of Portland’s offensive identity, and it’ll surely be missed. That being said, guys like Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson, and Donovan Clingan can all provide that. The athleticism will be a challenge to guard, but it’s really the size that is a major question mark. Clingan dominated the paint, but that was without Oso Ighodaro. The latter can limit and be that versatile big who can switch defensively. Both teams look different, but this being only two weeks fresh can play right into Phoenix’s hands for rewriting the story. item.title: How did Jaylen Brown possibly miss this wide-open layup?
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images How did Jaylen Brown possibly miss this wide-open layup? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With all the stars on the Philadelphia 76ers , Jaylen Brown is very much a leader. Along with LeBron James, he brings experience and accolades, and he knows how to set the example. That is until one brief embarrassing moment came on Wednesday as the 76ers took on the Detroit Pistons. It happened at the midway point of the 2nd quarter, when the 76ers led 48-31. Brown intercepted the pass and took it to the cup to lay it in. However, he lost his balance, bobbled the ball, and missed a wide-open layup. Even Brown was perplexed by how he could have done that, and he showed how he would have executed the layup while flashing a weary smile. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaylen Brown somehow misses a wide-open layup 👀 pic.twitter.com/fux1CsdAF0 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 5, 2026 Despite the mistake, the 76ers were up by a sizable margin going into the half, so no real harm was done. That is, if the Pistons make a dramatic comeback. At the half, the 76ers lead the Pistons 56-42. Brown leads the way with 23 points and is shooting 8-for-12 from the field. Meanwhile, the 76ers are off to an expected hot start at 7-1. So far, Brown is averaging 20.6 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game. Over the summer, Brown traded to the 76ers, who sent Paul George to the Boston Celtics. Brown made a name for himself in Boston. He helped lead the Celtics to an NBA championship in 2024, and Brown was named MVP . Now he is part of one of the most stacked NBA teams in recent memory that, frankly, has no excuse. So doing the little things, like making an open layup, goes a long way. item.title: Kenny Smith questions whether Spurs' three-guard lineup can last with Fox, Castle and Harper
item.description: ESPN analyst Kenny Smith questioned whether the Spurs can sustain their success with De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper starting together. (Bob Levey/Associated Press) The San Antonio Spurs may be finding success with their three-guard starting lineup, but NBA analyst Kenny Smith isn't convinced the approach can work for the long haul. During ESPN's "Inside the NBA" pregame show Wednesday, ahead of the Spurs' home matchup against the Dallas Mavericks, Smith questioned whether San Antonio can sustain its success with De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper sharing the floor. "I don't know if that's sustainable." Kenny Smith chimes in on the Spurs starting three guards ✍️ https://t.co/53Dv3vfg0S - NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 5, 2026 "I don't know if that's sustainable, honestly," Smith said. "I think one of the advantages that they had was that these three guards are really, really good. But they lack size." Smith's biggest concern centers on Castle, whose physicality and athleticism have made him a valuable part of San Antonio's backcourt. With the Spurs using three guards, Castle is tasked with playing more minutes at small forward, where he must contend with bigger opponents and take on additional rebounding responsibilities. ALSO READ: Streaking Spurs brace for Mavericks' Irving-Flagg one-two punch "Instead of having Castle running in and using his athleticism to get rebounds, he's boxing out to go get it," Smith said. Smith argued that Castle is better suited to shooting guard, where his strength gives him an advantage against smaller players. "I like when Castle's playing the guard spot and not the three, because he's so physical," Smith said. "There's not a lot of two guards in the league (like him)." San Antonio enters Wednesday's nationally televised matchup with Dallas at 5-2 and on a five-game winning streak, giving the Spurs another chance to test the lineup. item.title: Astros To Interview Former All-Star Infielder For Manager Vacancy
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 22: Manager Joe Espada #21 looks on before the game against the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on September 22, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Photo by Stephen Dunn/Getty Images Getty After their elimination from the American League Wild Card postseason round earlier this fall, the Houston Astros decided not to renew the contract of manager Joe Espada, who had been on the job since the start of the 2024 campaign. And while there is a notable list of names that the Astros are considering as his official successor, one name jumped to the top in the familiarity rankings of Houston baseball fans. According to Astros Insider Brian McTaggart, the club will be interviewing 2005 All-Star infielder Morgan Ensberg for the position of manager. The Houston Astros Will Interview Former All-Star Morgan Ensberg For Their Vacant Manager Position Getty Photo by Stephen Dunn/Getty Images According to McTaggart, Ensberg will be interviewed for the position that was vacated by Espada. “Source: the Astros will interview former Astros 3B Morgan Ensberg for their vacant managerial opening later this week,” McTaggart reported on X, formerly known as Twitter . “He is a former college teammate of GM Randy Flores and has spent the last three seasons managing the Durham Bulls , the Triple-A affiliate of the Rays.” In addition to Ensberg, the Astros will also be interviewing former St. Louis Cardinals All-Star Albert Pujols. Morgan Ensberg Is A Former Astros All-Star Ensberg was taken by the Astros in the ninth round of the 1998 MLB Draft, and he broke out in 2005, hitting .283 with 36 home runs and 101 RBI as the Astros reached the World Series. He was added to the National League All-Star team as an injury replacement and won a Silver Slugger Award at third base. Houston traded Ensberg to the San Diego Padres in July 2007. He later spent time with the New York Yankees and Cleveland Indians before signing with the Tampa Bay Rays in 2009. After being released during spring training, Ensberg retired following the season and began pursuing a career in broadcasting. He began coaching at UC San Diego in 2011 and 2012, working with hitters and infielders. He returned to the Astros organization in 2013 as a developmental coach before taking on several minor league roles. Ensberg became a manager in 2017 with Houston’s Tri-City affiliate and led the Buies Creek Astros to a Carolina League championship in 2018. Ensberg joined the Tampa Bay Rays organization in 2019, managing the Double-A Montgomery Biscuits to a franchise-record 88 wins and earning Southern League Manager of the Year honors. He later managed in the Arizona Fall League and became manager of the Triple-A Durham Bulls in 2024. He also managed Caribes de Anzoátegui in Venezuela during the 2024-25 season. item.description: Stanford tight end Dalton Schultz in the second half of an NCAA college football game, in Corvallis, Ore., Thursday, Oct. 26, 2017. (Timothy Gonzelez/AP) Former Stanford tight end Dalton Schultz got in on the excitement of Tuesday's "blue wave" of victories for the Democrats across the country with a simple message to soon-to-be-former Texas Gov. Greg Abbott: "Get f-ked." Schultz spent four seasons with the Cardinal from 2014 to 2017 and was an All-Pac-12 selection his senior year. Since then, however, he has played only on Texas teams throughout his professional career between the Dallas Cowboys (2018-2022) and the Houston Texans (2023-present). Another Texas constant was Abbott, who has been governor since 2015. But that will come to an end in January, as Abbott lost to his Democratic Party challenger Gina Hinojosa, who will become the first Latina governor in Texas history. Schultz clearly showed his preference in that race with an Instagram story posted early Wednesday morning that read, "Get f-ked," and tagged the outgoing governor. His next story was sharing a post about Hinojosa's victory. houston texas TE dalton schultz on his ig story … aaaaaand just like that i have a new favorite NFL player https://t.co/elPpXuSZ8t - claire de lune (@ClaireMPLS) November 4, 2026 This is not the first time the 30-year-old tight end has expressed his disdain for Abbott. When the Texas governor ordered Texas Department of Family and Protective Services to treat medically necessary gender-affirming care as child abuse, Schultz criticized the politician on social media. item.title: Deion Sanders resolves lawsuit over 'Prime' logos, case dismissed
item.description: Colorado football coach Deion Sanders has resolved a lawsuit that accused him of ripping off a graphic designer in Nebraska who claimed he created the “Prime” logo for Sanders and wasn’t compensated for it . Attorneys for Sanders and the designer, Alan Tipp, jointly asked a federal court in Nebraska to dismiss the case “with prejudice,” meaning Tipp’s complaint against Sanders can’t be refiled. Such joint stipulations typically mean the case was settled. “Plaintiff and Defendants shall each bear his or their own costs and attorneys' fees,” said the joint stipulation obtained by USA TODAY Sports. The court then noted on Nov. 3 “this case has been dismissed.” Terms of any settlement were not disclosed. Attorneys for Sanders and Tipp didn’t immediately answer questions about it from USA TODAY Sports. REQUIRED READING: Deion Sanders found an answer to Colorado’s problems hiding in plain sight What was this lawsuit against Deion Sanders about? Tipp filed the lawsuit in January 2025 , saying he created the P21ME and TRUTH logos for Sanders in 2011, which incorporate his old 21 jersey number with his nickname as Prime Time and Coach Prime. The P21ME logo later has been used on Blenders sunglasses, Nike products and other Colorado gear. The lawsuit named Sanders, Prime Time Enterprises and Sanders' business agency, SMAC Entertainment , as defendants and sought a judgment in excess of $75,000. Sanders’ attorneys denied the allegations in court records. Sanders also submitted a declaration with court in August , claiming the logos in question were part of his previous endorsement deal with the sports apparel company Under Armour. After Sanders ended his deal with Under Armour around July 2023, Sanders said he continued to use the trademarks. “No one at Under Armour, or anyone else, objected to my use of these logos until this lawsuit was filed,” Sanders said in his declaration. Sanders' attorneys said Tipp never owned any rights to logos Tipp’s complaint alleged he was induced to sign a “work-for-hire agreement” in which Tipp would relinquish his rights to the logos effective Aug. 1, 2011. He claims he signed the agreement based on false promises that he would be part of Sanders’ marketing team after that. Sanders’ attorneys were attempting to have the case thrown out of court with a summary judgment ruling before the joint filing to dismiss the case. Documents filed with Sanders’ legal team noted Tipp never owned copyrights to the logos. They said Under Armour engaged design company Eyeking to create sunglasses, with Tipp working as the director of design. “Tipp has never owned any rights, much less copyrights, in the logos,” Sanders' attorney stated. The claims against Prime Time Enterprises and SMAC Entertainment also have been dismissed. Sanders and Colorado next face Arizona State on the road on Nov. 7. MLB free agency began on Monday night at 5 p.m. ET, and there could be a sprint to sign players before the Dec. 1 lockout. Detroit Tigers Predicted to Sign Bryan Abreu Getty Tigers predicted to sign Bryan Abreu. The Tigers should look for bullpen help this offseason, and they could look to sign a veteran away from the Houston Astros . As free agency opened, MLB analyst Anthony Franco of MLBTradeRumors predicts the Tigers will sign Bryan Abreu to a two-year, $22 million deal. “The 2026 season started out in nightmare fashion,” the article read . “Abreu allowed runs in each of his first six appearances (and seven of his first nine; eight of his first 11). Through 11 appearances, he’d been tagged for 14 runs in 9 1/3 frames. His average fastball was sitting 95.1 mph — down more than two full miles from the preceding four-year average. Abreu began stringing together some scoreless outings, but his fastball velocity continued to dwindle. … ” It’s difficult to know any individual player’s motivations, but a shorter deal with an opt-out would give Abreu some safety net while still giving him the chance to return to the market next year having shown more consistency, better command and/or restored velocity. If he’s able to check some of those boxes, he’s young enough that he could line himself up for a truly big score on the open market — especially if he signs with a team that plans to use him as its closer. item.title: King's Academy volleyball wins first state championship in 20 years
item.description: WINTER HAVEN — To King's goes the crown. King's Academy volleyball took down Pine Crest, 25-15, 22-25, 25-21, 25-19 to win the Class 3A state championship, the program's first title in 20 years. More: King's Academy volleyball advances to first state final since 2007 The Lions (25-5) started off strong, taking control late in the first set with a 7-1 run that forced two timeouts ― to no avail ― by Pine Crest (20-11), further seizing the momentum with a 6-2 run to close out the first set. Pine Crest flipped the script during the second set, engineering their own 8-2 run to overcome the Lions' early surge. A timeout called by Avila seemed to settle King's Academy down but the Panthers won the roller-coaster race to 25 by taking advantage of a few late errors. With the match tied 1-1, King's Academy had to dig deep to find off a ferocious Pine Crest rally — though it was a picture-perfect start. A block for a kill and a clean tip-over from freshman Yasmin Nunes spurred high-energy cheers from the traveling King's fans, whose dance moves were rivaled only by the intensity of their celebrating as the Lions took control of the scoreboard. Despite facing a deficit of nearly 10 points, Pine Crest refused to yield easily, putting together a six-point run to draw within striking distance. With calls for "resiliency" from the crowd, the Lions found their ground and close things out for match point. King's Academy closed things out in the fourth behind a dominant set from Anabelle Bencosme, cementing the first state title in two decades. The Lions last appeared in a state title game in 2007, and they last won a championship the prior year in 2006. The win on Wednesday night ushers in a new era of King's Academy volleyball. item.title: Kevin Harvick Says Chase Elliott Influenced His Racing Mindset
item.description: Kevin Harvick reveals how Chase Elliott influenced his post-retirement racing career. Getty Kevin Harvick revealed that a conversation with Chase Elliott changed his mental approach to racing after his NASCAR career. The 2014 Cup Series champion retired from full-time NASCAR competition after the 2023 season but has since competed in a handful of Late Model races. Throughout his 20-plus career, Harvick won 60 career Cup Series races and a championship in 2014. Harvick is set to be inducted into the NASCAR Hall of Fame in January. Harvick Reveals Mindset-Changing Conversation With Elliott During an appearance on “The Dale Jr. Download,” Harvick revealed that following his final NASCAR Cup Series race in 2023 at Phoenix, he never wanted to get behind the wheel again. Harvick no longer wanted to carry the weight it took to be a top-notch driver. “When I got with Cup Racing, I was like, ‘Man, I don’t ever want to race again. I’m tired of being critiqued; I’m tired of the pressure; I’m tired of the responsibility,’” Harvick said. Harvick felt this way until he had a talk with Chase Elliott, the 2020 Cup Series champion and 23-time race winner, at the Chili Bowl Nationals . The conversation is something that stuck with Harvick in his views on racing after retirement. “One thing that really struck me a few years ago was Chase Elliott at the Chili Bowl. … He’s like, ‘I felt like I needed to step outside of my comfort zone and not worry about my result,’” Harvick recalled. The effect of the conversation with Elliott took a while for Harvick to come around to. “It just took me a little while to get myself to the point where I was like, ‘All right, well, I might go to the racetrack this week and get lapped,’ and I did,” Harvick said. However, Harvick recalls having a moment of clarity after a subpar performance. “I was kind of pissed and then I got out and I drank a beer and I thought about that conversation and I was like, ‘You know what? I had a hell of a time.’ Yeah, it’d be really cool to win some. We won some of those races and ran up front in some and got our ass kicked in some, but they are all pretty fun,” Harvick said. Harvick’s Changed Outlook on Racing: ‘Here to Have Fun’ Harvick continues to run select Late Model races today but does not put the same pressure on himself as he did during his NASCAR career. When there is not as much stock put into the effort, Harvick said that is when he and his team are enjoying themselves the most at the racetrack. “I’m like, ‘Hey, I’m here to have fun.’ We’ll put an effort towards it but probably not going to go overboard with the effort to really get extreme with it. We have the greatest time ever,” Harvick said. After his NASCAR retirement, Harvick became a TV analyst for NASCAR on FOX alongside Mike Joy and Clint Bowyer. It's been an interesting start to the season for the Boston Celtics , as they've played decent basketball on both ends but just don't look to be the best team in the Eastern Conference by any means. At 5-2, the Celtics have to feel like they've done a decent job, though there's also an argument that they've blown some opportunities to win games they should have. Regardless, I trust the Celtics to figure things out year in and year out, even with some of the players who are currently struggling. One of those guys is Mitchell Robinson, who they were able to poach from the New York Knicks in free agency. Getting Robinson from the defending world champion Knicks was a great addition, at least on paper. However, Robinson is playing just 19.3 minutes per game and, unfortunately, hasn't looked to be the player that he was expected to be. As a result, it was recently suggested that if things continue to go south, the Celtics could look to move on from him sooner rather than later. “We’re not suggesting that Robinson is headed to the trade block, but if this looks to be a bad fit when late January comes around, it is fair to wonder–again, this is speculation–whether the Celtics might get Robinson onto the market sooner rather than later, before his value tanks. His contract is reasonable (three years, $47 million) and there would likely be teams willing to overlook a bad stretch in Boston and gamble that Robinson could recapture his Knicks mojo if he landed elsewhere,” Sean Deveney wrote . Robinson's fit with the Celtics seemed very obvious when they signed him. Boston's idea was that it gets up a ton of three-point shots, and with Robinson as the league's best offensive rebounder, it would be a match made in heaven because the team would get more offensive possessions. However, Robinson hasn't been able to grab rebounds at any level to start the year, averaging just 4.5 total so far.
